pr_title: Prevent ActionDispatch::ServerTiming from overwriting existing header value
pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes #45607 

Tiny fix, if a middleware adds anything to the `Server-Timing` header, and is down the chain from `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming`, the value it set will be overwritten, this PR changes this behaviour, so that `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` appends its entries instead.
pr_comments: Could you squash the commits into one?
Done, and, not sure if there can ever be no ActiveSupport Notification events in a response, but I changed the code slightly to handle that too.

> Issue for this PR: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45607

Could you change this to read "Fixes #45607", then it will automatically close the issue when the PR is merged.
@jonathanhefner All the suggestions were great, thanks for reviewing.

issue_context.title: `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` overwrites instead of appending to the `Server-Timing` header.
issue_context.body:
`ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` overwrites instead of appending to the `Server-Timing` header.

In an application this can be solved by inserting the middleware before the `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming`, however in a library it is potentially difficult to consistently insert the middleware so that it executes after `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` or at the right time if `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` is not present in the middlewares stack.

Our team would like to submit a PR which improves this behaviour and if possible (and needed) back-port it to Rails `6.x` and `5.x`. The change is really simple and straightforward, basically in `ActionDispatch::ServerTiming` we append to `Server-Timing` if it already has a value.

### Steps to reproduce
Add a Railtie in a fresh Rails 7.0.3 app:

```ruby
module MyServerTiming
  class MyMiddleware
    def initialize(app)
      @app = app
    end

    def call(env)
      status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
      headers["Server-Timing"] = [headers["Server-Timing"], %(myprop;desc="something";dur=1)].compact.join(", ")
      [status, headers, body]
    end
  end

  class Railtie < ::Rails::Railtie
    config.before_initialize do |app|
      app.middleware.use MyMiddleware
    end
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
Server-Timing header does not include `myprop;desc="something";dur=1`.

### Actual behavior
Server-Timing header should include `myprop` entry.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: `7.0.3.1`
**Ruby version**: `3.1`, but it should not matter for the purpose of this issue
comments:
> Our team would like to submit a PR which improves this behaviour

Yes, please do make a PR 👍 

> if possible (and needed) back-port it to Rails `6.x` and `5.x`

FYI server timing was added in Rails 7. I don't think this would get backported as it's not really a bug fix.

review_comments:
Should we assert that the server timing middleware also still adds its headers?

```suggestion
      assert_match(/entry;desc="description"/, @response.headers["Server-Timing"])
      assert_match(/start_processing.action_controller;dur=\w+/, @response.headers["Server-Timing"])
```
